Definition: to join (literally or figuratively); specifically (by means of spells) to fascinate
BiblicalUsage: Chabar means to join, to bind together — and joining cuts both ways. The kings of the plain joined together in the vale of Siddim, the curtains of the tabernacle were coupled together into one covering, the law forbids the charmer who joins himself to spirits, and Jehoshaphat joined himself with wicked Ahaziah, who did very wickedly.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe joining is a spiritual act: what you join yourself to, you become. Curtains joined together make a dwelling for God, and a king joined to a wicked king joins himself to the wickedness.
